Concepts & schemas — the building blocks

The building blocks, from raw dataset to composed output. Each block: what it IS, its schema shape, a real example harvested live from the repos, and where it is defined. This is the conceptual companion to the Explorer (which shows how specific instances are wired together).

1 Source manifest 225 in repo manifests/sources/*.yaml (rnd-computational-biology-oncology-data-catalog)

A source manifest is one YAML record in the data-catalog describing an external dataset received whole (DepMap, TCGA, GENIE, gnomAD). It records the S3 location, per-file MD5 + size, license, provenance pipeline, and data subject — the catalog is the source-of-record for WHAT data exists and WHERE, never the bytes themselves. Everything downstream reads a manifest to find its data.

2 Derived manifest 275 in repo manifests/derived/*.yaml (rnd-computational-biology-oncology-data-catalog)

A derived manifest describes a team-produced, query-optimized product built from one or more sources — a gene-SORTED parquet on S3. It pins the producing git commit + notebook (reproducibility), the parquet schema and sort key (so readers do a one-gene predicate- pushdown read), and `derived_from` (the lineage edge back to sources). `cited_by` is auto-populated, forming an implicit do-not-delete graph.

3 Method (analysis-methods) 5 in repo schemas/methods/*.summary.schema.json (rnd-computational-biology-oncology-target-contracts)

A method is deterministic compute — `fn(target=, indication=) -> summary dict` — that reads a catalog product and emits NUMBERS and categorical LABELS, never a verdict. Its output validates against a per-card summary schema at compose time, so schema drift is caught before it reaches an evidence package. Methods live in the analysis-methods repo; a card names the method that produces it.

4 Card (evidence contract) 146 in repo cards/*.card.yaml (rnd-computational-biology-oncology-target-contracts)

A card is the declarative contract for one piece of evidence, and the hinge of the whole framework. Its identity is (measurement_type x entity_grain) — gates PULL a measurement type, data PUSHES a provider, so a new dataset slots in without touching gate logic. It binds the product it reads (`required_inputs`), the method that produces it (`methods`), and the closed-vocabulary labels it emits (`outputs.summary_fields`). Cards emit descriptive labels only; interpretation lives in the rules layer.

5 Interpretation rule 8 in repo interpretation-rules/*.rules.yaml (rnd-computational-biology-oncology-target-contracts)

An interpretation rule maps one card LABEL to a per-modality SIGNAL, firing a named `rule_id` — e.g. "when dependency_class == common_essential -> small_molecule: killer". This is the only place a descriptive label becomes a therapeutic signal. Rules never decide a verdict; they produce the fired-rule set that a resolver reduces.

6 Resolver (verdict ladder) 10 in repo resolvers/*.resolver.yaml (rnd-computational-biology-oncology-target-contracts)

A resolver reduces the SET of fired rule_ids to one verdict per gate. It is an ordered precedence ladder that pattern-matches only over rule_ids — deliberately not Turing-complete (no arithmetic; that lives in the card/method). It emits a verdict token plus a `driving_rule_id` provenance anchor and a `default` (usually insufficient) so exhaustiveness is provable. A single shared interpreter runs every gate, so verdicts are byte-stable.

gatestringrequiredThe sub-skill / gate this resolver governs (matches the SUB_SKILLS short, e.g. 'dependency', 'expression', 'surface_modality').
versionstringrequiredSemVer of THIS resolver spec. A verdict-precedence change is a reviewable contract bump, not a silent code diff.
descriptionstringoptional
resolvearrayrequiredORDERED precedence ladder — first matching rung wins (the precedence, now visible). Each rung fires a verdict when its fired-set predicate m
defaultstringrequiredThe verdict when NO rung matches (typically 'insufficient'). driving_rule_id is null for the default. Making the default EXPLICIT is what le
evaluationoptionalHow the shared interpreter evaluates this ladder. `first_match` (DEFAULT when absent — back-compat): the earliest matching rung wins (implic
first_match match_all_reduce

7 Skill (question + composition) 27 in repo skills/*/SKILL.md (rnd-computational-biology-oncology-claude-oncology-skills)

A skill answers one biological question by composing a set of cards, firing their rules, and resolving a verdict. Its SKILL.md `composition` block declares data_mode, phase, cards_used, rules_scope, and status. The composed target-profile skill fans out to ~13 focused skills, inherits each sub-verdict from the shared resolver spine (never re-resolves), then adds LLM synthesis on top.

8 Evidence package / synthesis 4 in repo */*/ep-*/evidence_package.json (rnd-computational-biology-oncology-data-products)

An evidence package is the terminal composed output for one target x indication. It carries the deterministic sub-verdicts, per-card evidence, governance (which manifest versions were read, with staleness flags), and a synthesis block. The LLM narration rides in DISTINCT schema slots tagged `_source: llm_synthesized`, and its recommendation is clamped by a fail-closed gate — so narrative can never move an auditable verdict.

Objective → axis → card ontology

Canonical objective→axis→card ontology (target_profiling_axes v1.1.0) — the decision questions a full target profile must answer, the evidence axis for each, its framework coverage standing, and the home / foreign skills that report into it. Click a skill to open it in the Explorer.

coverage: captured · partial · blind · license_blocked · out_of_scope

Necessity — “is this real, actionable biology?” (ANY-OF, modality-independent)

axis · questioncoveragehome skillforeign consumersfacets / reports-intoconditioned by
expression
Is the target expressed / present in the tumor?
capturedtumor-presence · 17cfunctional-requirement · 16c surface-modality-fit · 24c—modality, subtype, molecular_form
selectivity
Is the target selective for tumor vs normal (adjacent=efficacy; population=safety)?
capturedtumor-selectivity · 14csurface-modality-fit · 24c—modality, subtype, molecular_form
dependency
Is the target a functional dependency / driver, and in which context?
partialfunctional-requirement · 16c—facets: mutation_stratified, expression_correlation, crispr_rnai_concordance, chemical_genetic_concordance, synthetic_lethal_partners, dependency_predictability, subtype_fit—
mechanism advisory
What is the target's network position / MoA hook / PD marker?
partialmechanism-and-pharmacology · 5c———
genomic_alteration
How is the target genomically altered (SNV / CN / fusion), and which class drives?
capturedgenomic-alteration-profile · 26con-target-safety-liability · 15c→ reports into: dependencysubtype
cis_coherence advisory wired
Does the target's OWN locus feature (copy-number / promoter methylation) explain its OWN expression AND its OWN dependency — a coherent cis-driven addiction, or co-occurring but mechanistically-independent axes?
partialcis-feature-coherence · 9c—→ reports into: dependencysubtype, molecular_form

Sufficiency — “will it become a drug in this modality?” (per-lens)

axis · questioncoveragehome skillforeign consumersfacets / reports-intoconditioned by
tractability_sm
Is the target druggable by a small molecule (compound exists + agrees with genetics)?
partialtractability-small-molecule · 8c——modality, molecular_form
surface_modality
Does surface biology support a biologics modality (ADC / TCE / antibody)?
partialsurface-modality-fit · 24c——modality, molecular_form
safety
Is the target intolerant of loss-of-function / does normal-tissue liability threaten a therapeutic window?
partialon-target-safety-liability · 15c——modality
differentiation
Is the target differentiated (co-mutation landscape, precedent, biomarker definability)?
partialdifferentiation-landscape · 9c——subtype
translational unbuilt
Can the nomination be preclinically validated (patient-derived models, PD/imaging assays, combination/resistance)?
blindtranslational-readiness · 4c———
combination_vulnerability planned_consolidation
What does the target depend on / combine with RELATIONALLY — synthetic-lethal partners, measured dual-KO co-dependencies, combination co-targets under inhibition, and resistance mediators?
partialcombination-and-vulnerability · 4c—→ reports into: dependencysubtype
